ch-1rvx.title: Plants: fruit trees near big lakes
ch-1rvx.summary: Outside the Martigny valley, fruit trees are most likely near Lake Constance, then northwest of Lake Geneva.

ch-5c2b.title: Sign: blue street name with rounded side edges
ch-5c2b.summary: Blue street signs with rounded edges on the sides, unique to Sankt Gallen.

ch-6CVU.title: Houses: big, thick roofs arched underneath
ch-6CVU.summary: Large houses with thick roofs that curve like an arch underneath are common around Bern.

ch-9CSb.title: Sign: blue main-road
ch-9CSb.summary: Direction sign colour tells the road type: blue for main roads and white for side roads. Big place names are often on blue, small ones on white, though big cities can appear on white too.

ch-9xai.title: Landscape: limestone cliffs poking from
ch-9xai.summary: Exposed limestone rocks sticking out of forested hills are common in the Jura mountains.

ch-ARS4.title: Sign: speed limit wording follows regional
ch-ARS4.summary: The text on speed limit signs changes with the official language of the region.

ch-DapV.title: Bollard: thick wooden, square or round
ch-DapV.summary: In the canton of Valais, thick wooden bollards, square or cylindrical, are common.

ch-EEdr.title: Postal codes: first digits rise west to east
ch-EEdr.summary: The first digits of postal codes are a good region clue. They generally increase from west to east.

ch-FOTA.title: Landscape: very mountainous south
ch-FOTA.summary: The south is extremely mountainous with long thin valleys. The north is mostly big farmland on flat or rolling ground, with forested hills in the distance.

ch-H9pK.title: Sign: olive green posts, borders and backs
ch-H9pK.summary: Olive green signposts, sign borders and sign backs are found in Basel-Landschaft.

ch-JMIW.title: Chevron: black with white arrow
ch-JMIW.summary: Black chevrons with a white arrow, rarely white with a black arrow. Austrian chevrons are red and white or red and yellow.

differs.how: Austrian chevrons are red and white or red and yellow

ch-JZSb.title: Google car: rare Gen 2, near two cantons
ch-JZSb.summary: The older Gen 2 camera (lower quality) is very limited: mostly near the Bern-Valais border and a few short stretches in Schaffhausen. Ski resorts with Gen 2 snow coverage are not counted.

ch-JkUC.title: Sign: large town entry signs
ch-JkUC.summary: These large town entry signs are sometimes seen in the canton of Vaud.

ch-K1Ul.title: Road: yellow-painted pedestrian crossings
ch-K1Ul.summary: Yellow-painted crossings exist in Europe only here and in Liechtenstein.

ch-KVPw.title: Houses: all-stone with white painted trim
ch-KVPw.summary: In Graubünden, houses entirely of stone with mostly white decorative painted details around windows and edges.

ch-Oo4G.title: Language: four languages by region
ch-Oo4G.summary: German, French, Italian and Romansh are spoken in their own regions, with some bilingual areas near borders. Unlike Germany and Austria, Swiss German doesn't use ß.

differs.how: Swiss German has no ß; Germany uses it
Swiss German has no ß; Austria uses it

ch-PEET.title: Sign: round grey metal border on direction
ch-PEET.summary: Road signs commonly have a round grey metal border. Liechtenstein's direction signs are nearly identical, and Denmark has somewhat similar metal borders on some.

differs.how: Only some direction signs have similar metal borders

ch-V7Ou.title: Bollard: reflectors on roadside fences instead
ch-V7Ou.summary: In Glarus, reflectors are often attached to fences along the road instead of bollards.

ch-WZTx.title: Road lines: long dashed yellow
ch-WZTx.summary: Long dashed yellow road lines are a good clue. They are also common in Liechtenstein.

ch-XO5x.title: Road: bike symbol with simple person on two
ch-XO5x.summary: Around Geneva and in the valley between Martigny and Lake Geneva, the painted bike symbol is a simple person on top of two separate wheels. Elsewhere it's a more detailed bike.

ch-YE3t.title: Houses: elaborate red timber frames, northeast
ch-YE3t.summary: Elaborate timber frames, often painted red, are in the northeast. Simpler timber frames in other colours appear elsewhere.

ch-aYNF.title: Houses: warm-coloured stone, wood, shutters
ch-aYNF.summary: Stone buildings in light, warm colours with wooden parts and details, tiled gable roofs, and wooden shutters that open horizontally in two halves.

ch-bd1S.title: Sign: large blue street name on low double post
ch-bd1S.summary: Large blue street signs on a low double signpost, like Danish direction signs, in Basel.

differs.how: Danish direction signs look similar but are not street names

ch-e1U8.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing, seven stripes
ch-e1U8.summary: A pedestrian sign with seven stripes, almost unique in Europe, shaped as a tall blue rectangle instead of the usual square. Liechtenstein uses identical signs.

ch-e2jj.title: Road dividers: types by region (graphic)
ch-e2jj.summary: Several kinds of road dividers appear across the country, with distribution shown in the graphic (by quarksauce). Click to enlarge.

ch-efcd.title: Landscape: mountainous south, lower north
ch-efcd.summary: Elevation is key. The south is extremely mountainous, while the north mostly has smaller mountains and hills.

ch-fLRI.title: Landscape: hilly, big lake south
ch-fLRI.summary: Hilly but not mountainous land, with a large lake to the south and tall mountains on the far side, means you are very likely north of Lake Geneva.

ch-hdVS.title: Plants: many small fruit trees in a wide flat
ch-hdVS.summary: The Martigny valley has the most fruit plantations in the country: lots of small fruit trees in a wide, flat valley with big mountains either side.

ch-hhwq.title: Sign: two-letter canton abbreviations
ch-hhwq.summary: The two-letter abbreviation of the canton often shows on town entry signs, so learning them helps region-guessing. An unblurred plate starts with the canton letters.

ch-jQTD.title: Houses: living house joined to barn at 90
ch-jQTD.summary: Around Appenzell, a large living house is joined to a long barn at a right angle, with the house front split into small squares each holding a window.

ch-kRj5.title: Sign: bus stop with thick metal post around it
ch-kRj5.summary: Bus stop signs with a thick metal post going around them, unique to this country.

ch-lPuj.title: Bollard: black-white, wedge or round top
ch-lPuj.summary: Black and white bollards with white or grey reflectors, either wedge-shaped or cylindrical with a rounded top. Liechtenstein has almost identical round ones.

ch-lm-2231.title: Sign: speed limit "limite generale"
ch-lm-2231.summary: Italian is spoken in the south near Italy. Speed signs saying "limite generale" show you are in the Italian-speaking part.

ch-lm-2234.title: Sign: speed limit "limite générale"
ch-lm-2234.summary: French is spoken in the west. Speed signs saying "limite générale" (with accent) show you are in the French-speaking part.

ch-lm-2235.title: Language: Romansh words like ospidal, scoula
ch-lm-2235.summary: A Romansh word mixed with German or Italian means Romansh country: ospidal (hospital), scoula (school), bainvgnieu (welcome), limita generala (speed limit), restorant, parc naziunal, attenziun (warning).

ch-lm-740383.title: Sign: blue street name, white edge, four dots
ch-lm-740383.summary: Zurich street signs are blue with a white edge and four thick dots in the corners.

ch-lm-783095.title: Language: German region, ss instead of ß
ch-lm-783095.summary: German is the most spoken language, mostly in the centre and north. Place names on the map hint at the language. Swiss German writes ss instead of ß, so Strasse not Straße.

differs.how: Germany writes ß, Swiss German writes ss
Austria writes ß, Swiss German writes ss

ch-lm-783096.title: Language: French region in the west
ch-lm-783096.summary: French is the second most spoken language, in the west. Place names on the map hint at the language, and borders are sometimes bilingual.

ch-lm-783097.title: Language: Italian region in the south
ch-lm-783097.summary: Italian is spoken in the south, close to Italy. Place names on the map hint at the language, and borders are sometimes bilingual.

ch-lm-791259.title: Houses: wide, very low-pitched roofs
ch-lm-791259.summary: Wide houses with strikingly low-pitched roofs and many windows, in the cantons of Jura and Neuchâtel and the north of Bern. A half-hipped variant exists.

ch-lm-791260.title: Roofs: small bump finial on the ridge
ch-lm-791260.summary: A small bump-shaped finial on the roof, common in Vaud, Fribourg, Geneva, Neuchâtel and western Valais, very rarely in Bern.

ch-lm-791261.title: Roofs: chimney right by the gable end
ch-lm-791261.summary: Chimneys on the small gable of half-hipped roofs, or very near the gable on hipped roofs, mostly in the west (Vaud and Fribourg), with rare exceptions.

ch-lm-791262.title: Houses: low roof with balcony in the gable
ch-lm-791262.summary: In Neuchâtel, wide low-roofed houses sometimes have a balcony built into the gable, and sometimes wood-clad gable arches.

ch-lm-791263.title: Houses: wide recessed entrance
ch-lm-791263.summary: A devant-huis is a traditional wide, recessed entranceway in the canton of Jura, often with vertical timber planks above the entrance.

ch-lm-791364.title: Houses: arched gates, now flats or shops
ch-lm-791364.summary: Houses with arched gates in the north and west, once entrances to farmhouses and barns, now often hiding modern flats, shops or restaurants.

ch-lm-791365.title: Houses: wide tent-like roofs with deep overhang
ch-lm-791365.summary: Strikingly wide, bulky houses with deeply overhanging tent-like roofs, in the northern half of the canton of Bern.

ch-lm-791366.title: Houses: half-hipped roof
ch-lm-791366.summary: Half-hipped roofs with a thick arch under the gable, giving a bulky look, in Bern and neighbouring cantons.

ch-lm-791367.title: Walls: pale yellow bricks, west to east strip
ch-lm-791367.summary: Pale yellow bricks in a wide strip from Bern to St. Gallen. Houses can be all brick or mix them with red decorative bricks or timber.

ch-lm-791368.title: Houses: wavy gable arches
ch-lm-791368.summary: Gables in Lucerne have arches like those in Bern, but wavy instead of simple semicircles.

ch-lm-791590.title: Walls: miniature roofs over windows
ch-lm-791590.summary: Houses with tiny roofs over windows, in the area on the map. Sometimes they run along the whole wall, sometimes just over the windows.

ch-lm-791591.title: Walls: irregular stones smeared with light
ch-lm-791591.summary: Walls of irregular stone plastered with thick, light mortar smeared over the stones, in Valais, Ticino and the Italian-speaking parts of Graubünden.

ch-lm-791592.title: Houses: several small roofs on the gable end
ch-lm-791592.summary: Several small roofs on the gable end, in the mapped areas (rarely elsewhere). They can continue along the side walls.

ch-lm-791593.title: Walls: wooden shingle cladding
ch-lm-791593.summary: Traditional wooden shingle walls in a central belt from St. Gallen in the east to Valais in the west. Shingles can be rounded or angular.

ch-lm-791594.title: Walls: pastel-coloured shingles
ch-lm-791594.summary: Shingle walls in pastel colours, mostly in the east and rarer towards the west. Shingles can be round, rectangular, diamond or cone shaped.

ch-lm-791595.title: Roofs: rectangular metal panels
ch-lm-791595.summary: Rectangular metal panels sometimes roof houses and sheds in Valais and Graubünden, especially the northwest of Graubünden.

ch-lm-791596.title: Roofs: chimney at the gable end
ch-lm-791596.summary: Houses with chimneys at the gable end are found in the central valleys of Ticino.

ch-lm-791597.title: Roofs: double pitch, lower part shallower
ch-lm-791597.summary: Gable roofs in two slopes, with the lower part at a shallower angle, in the mapped area.

ch-lm-791598.title: Roofs: downward-pointing ends of beams
ch-lm-791598.summary: Downward-pointing finials on the ends of the load-bearing beams of gable roofs, in the mapped areas. Shapes range from rectangular to ornamental.

ch-lm-791599.title: Houses: shutterless window rows with
ch-lm-791599.summary: A distinctive house style in the Appenzell cantons and nearby St. Gallen: rows of shutterless windows on the gable side with rectangular panels beneath and between. A baroque variant in towns has a curved roof and decorated panels.

ch-lm-791737.title: Houses: timber frame, thick arches, tent roofs
ch-lm-791737.summary: Timber-frame houses occur in two main regions. In the west they often have thick arched gables, triangular supports under the roof and big tent roofs.

ch-lm-791738.title: Roofs: very flat, barely sloped
ch-lm-791738.summary: Most houses in Valsot in the far east have very flat roofs with a barely visible slope, and nearby villages too.

ch-lm-791739.title: Houses: timber frame, double-pitch, big dormers
ch-lm-791739.summary: In the northeastern timber-frame region: double-pitched gable roofs, big dormers, and sometimes long buildings running along the street.

ch-lm-791740.title: Roofs: slate in neat rows
ch-lm-791740.summary: In Ticino slate roofs are sometimes laid in neat rows, unlike the more irregular pattern on other Swiss slate roofs.

ch-lm-791741.title: Roofs: slate, three southern cantons
ch-lm-791741.summary: Slate roofs are common in the three southern cantons: Valais, Ticino and Graubünden.

ch-lm-791742.title: Walls: sgraffito patterns carved in plaster
ch-lm-791742.summary: In Graubünden, sgraffito: patterns carved into fresh light plaster to show the darker layer beneath.

ch-lm-791743.title: Walls: more colourful sgraffito
ch-lm-791743.summary: Val Müstair in the far east of Graubünden paints houses in a variant of sgraffito with more colours and different designs. Normal sgraffito also occurs.

ch-lm-791744.title: Houses: tall, narrow dark wood with balconies
ch-lm-791744.summary: In the north-south valleys of Valais, dark-wood houses are tall and narrow, often slate-roofed with several balconies, decorative fretwork and visible interlocking log corners.

ch-lm-791745.title: Houses: dark wood with a curved support under
ch-lm-791745.summary: In Obwalden and nearby, dark-wood houses have a curved structural support along a wall holding up an overhanging upper floor, sometimes with a balcony.

ch-lm-791746.title: Houses: wide dark wood, carved dates
ch-lm-791746.summary: Wide dark-wood houses in southern Bern and Vaud and northwest Valais, with carvings and inscriptions (e.g. build year), decorated eaves, one or two staircases, covered side balconies, and wooden versions of the thick arched roofs.

ch-lm-791747.title: Roofs: large diamond-shaped slate slabs
ch-lm-791747.summary: Roofs with large diamond-shaped slate slabs, across central Valais.

ch-lm-791749.title: Walls: timber and white plaster
ch-lm-791749.summary: Houses mixing timber and white plaster, usually one-third of one and two-thirds of the other, most common in Valais and northern Graubünden.

ch-lm-791750.title: Barns: wavy or semicircular gable arch
ch-lm-791750.summary: Barns in Lucerne can have a wavy gable arch or, unlike houses, a semicircular one. Some have a half-hipped roof with a tiny triangular gable, and some a vehicle entrance.

ch-lm-791751.title: Barns: gable covered in terracotta or grey
ch-lm-791751.summary: In western Fribourg, barns with gables covered in terracotta tiles or sometimes grey diamond-shaped ones. A variant has an extra vehicle entrance.

ch-lm-791752.title: Barns: low-pitched roofs like local houses
ch-lm-791752.summary: Barns in Jura and Neuchâtel often have low-pitched roofs like local houses, usually part of the same building but sometimes separate, with large double doors for vehicles.

ch-lm-791753.title: Barns: wide with tent-like roofs
ch-lm-791753.summary: Strikingly wide barns with tent-like roofs, like local houses, in the northern half of Bern. A variant has a covered vehicle entrance.

ch-lm-791754.title: Barns: house and barn fused together
ch-lm-791754.summary: In the Entlebuch region, the far south of Lucerne, house and barn are fused into one building, especially striking from the front.

ch-lm-791755.title: Houses: gables covered with red tiles
ch-lm-791755.summary: Houses with gables covered in striking red tiles are frequent in northeastern Vaud and western Fribourg, with rare cases elsewhere.

ch-lm-791756.title: Barns: double-pitch roof, lower part shallower
ch-lm-791756.summary: Barns in the mapped area can have double-pitched roofs, the lower part at a shallower angle, like houses nearby.

ch-lm-791757.title: Barns: bulky, half-hipped, timber supports
ch-lm-791757.summary: In Bern, barns mirror local houses: bulky, often half-hipped roofs, sometimes timber supports. A variant has a vehicle entrance, and sometimes the barn attaches directly to the house.

ch-lm-791758.title: Barns: attached to house in T or L shape
ch-lm-791758.summary: Barns in Appenzell and around are often attached to the house in a T or L layout, easy to spot from far away.

ch-lm-791759.title: Barns: prominent transverse roof below the
ch-lm-791759.summary: In Zug and neighbouring cantons, barns with a prominent transverse roof extending below the main gable.

ch-lm-791760.title: Barns: diamond lattice pattern on doors
ch-lm-791760.summary: A diamond lattice pattern on barn doors, found in Thurgau and Zurich.

ch-lm-791822.title: Barns: wood with concrete or stone corners
ch-lm-791822.summary: Barns mixing wood with concrete or stone, usually at the corners, in Valais and Graubünden. Exposed round beams only occur in Graubünden.

ch-lm-791823.title: Huts: interlocking rectangular logs
ch-lm-791823.summary: Wooden huts in Valais are often built from interlocking rectangular logs visible from outside.

ch-lm-791824.title: Granary: raised wooden barn on stilts with
ch-lm-791824.summary: Raccards are raised wooden granaries of Valais, on short stilts each topped with a round stone slab to keep rodents out.

ch-lm-791825.title: Huts: round beams
ch-lm-791825.summary: Huts in Graubünden often use round beams, for the whole structure or just the gable. Huts with rectangular beams also exist there.

ch-lm-791826.title: Huts: mainly stone, slate roofs
ch-lm-791826.summary: Huts in Ticino are often mainly stone, with roofs of slate tiles.

ch-lm-791827.title: Barns: wooden upper-floor balconies
ch-lm-791827.summary: Upper-floor wooden balconies are common on barns in southwestern Valais.

ch-lm-791828.title: Shrines: colourful Catholic shrines
ch-lm-791828.summary: Catholic shrines in Ticino are often colourful with religious imagery, and may have slate roofs.

ch-lm-791829.title: Churches: onion-shaped gable around the clock
ch-lm-791829.summary: Church towers with an onion-shaped gable around the clock face, in a central band from Bern in the west to Glarus in the east.

ch-lm-791830.title: Churches: main spire with several small spires
ch-lm-791830.summary: Church towers with a main spire surrounded by small spires, most common in the west, especially around Neuchâtel, occasionally elsewhere.

ch-lm-791831.title: Churches: onion domes
ch-lm-791831.summary: Onion domes on churches are a strong sign of the non-French-speaking regions, with exceptions.

ch-lm-791832.title: Churches: rooster on the steeple
ch-lm-791832.summary: A rooster atop a church steeple usually means a Protestant church and strongly suggests the French-speaking part, with isolated exceptions.

ch-lm-791833.title: Churches: simple triangular gable tower
ch-lm-791833.summary: Church towers with a simple triangular gable are most frequent in the north and centre.

ch-lm-791834.title: Churches: tower with triangular gables on
ch-lm-791834.summary: Church towers whose walls form upward-pointing triangular gables on several sides, most often in the northeast.

ch-nUOq.title: Landscape: flat land
ch-nUOq.summary: A fairly flat landscape with a long chain of medium forested mountains to the northwest means you are likely south of the Jura mountains.

ch-pdKy.title: Houses: smooth orange-yellow stone
ch-pdKy.summary: Italian-style architecture means the Italian-speaking south, mainly Ticino: very smooth orange-yellow stone walls, several floors, orange or brown tiled roofs, and green or brown shutters.

ch-pzZV.title: Houses: grey four-floor buildings
ch-pzZV.summary: Downtown Bern: grey-toned buildings, usually four floors, with large, somewhat rounded openings lined up along the ground floor.

ch-q9q8.title: Coverage: train coverage on a mountain railway
ch-q9q8.summary: In Graubünden, distinctive train coverage on the Bernina Express tracks, running around most of the canton down to Tirano in Italy.

ch-srYV.title: Camera: low-cam, big car blur, low viewpoint
ch-srYV.summary: All car coverage is low-cam: the camera sits lower than usual, so the car blur is much bigger, roads look wider and things are seen from a low angle. Japan and Liechtenstein also always have this.

ch-vKu1.title: Landscape: rock walls, mostly Jura
ch-vKu1.summary: Rock walls are mainly in the Jura mountains, but also in the Alps, particularly in the Italian-speaking parts.

ch-wLZ9.title: Plate: all white, no blue strip, short front
ch-wLZ9.summary: All-white plates with no blue EU strip. The front plate is very short, and the rear is long or tall. A red country emblem is on the left and a canton emblem on the right.

ch-waGu.title: Sign: white or blue town entry, metal frame
ch-waGu.summary: Town entry signs are usually white or blue with a metal frame. The back often shows distances to nearby big cities, and the bottom often shows the canton abbreviation, especially near canton borders.

ch-xSSR.title: Landscape: wide lake northeast, low terrain
ch-xSSR.summary: A wide lake to the northeast in fairly low land is Lake Constance (Bodensee). You are probably close to the shore.
